StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterShuffle.rationale: Same hook, same order of operations: select Amount cards from the DRAW pile and move them to the hand (StratagemPower.cs:24-27 vs powers.py:3738-3745). The selection goes through CardSelectCmd.from_pile (cmds.py:532-542) -> CombatState.select_cards (combat.py:560-581), which is the sim's modelled player-choice seam -- it delegates to an installed card_selector (the conformance replay, the RL policy) and falls back to a uniform random pick only when none is installed, which is the same treatment power/entropy's CardSelectCmd.FromHand gets. C# passes CardSelectorPrefs(base.SelectionScreenPrompt, base.Amount); the sim's purpose string 'from_draw' stands in for the prompt. The move is a pile transfer, not a draw, on both sides -- C# CardPileCmd.Add(item, PileType.Hand) at :26, the sim remove/append at :3744-3745 -- so neither fires on_card_drawn and power/automation and power/confused do not see these cards. Correct.

guards.rationale: The sim's on_shuffle carries the player (hooks.py:433) and the sim uses it as the pile owner rather than as a filter (powers.py:3736-3739). Tautology in single-player.

guards.what: The sim ADDS a MAX_HAND_SIZE break
guards.rationale: powers.py:3742-3743 stops moving cards once the hand is full. C# relies on CardPileCmd.Add's own handling of CardPile.MaxCardsInHand (the constant CombatManager.cs:671 also clamps the turn-1 innate draw against), so the cap exists on both sides -- what differs is only where it is enforced. Defensive, not divergent. Third-file citation, not hashed here.

AfterShuffle fires when the discard pile is shuffled into an empty draw pile, which mid-draw means cards move back into the hand while the draw is still in progress. Both sides fire from the shuffle site itself, so the interleaving is the same; the sim's reshuffle site is player.reshuffle_discard_into_draw (player.py:199ff), whose own pile-limbo handling for a card mid-OnPlay (player.py:203-206) is the PROMPT.md bug class 7 fix and is not this power's concern.
Neither side ticks or removes it. Both agree.
